symptom: A business event message attribute named like a member the event entity inherits from BusinessEvents.PublishedBusinessEvent (`message Msg (EventId: long, ...)` on a PBE_ entity extending it) passed check and exec; mxbuild then reported "The Business Events attribute 'EventId' is not present on the entity." on the service (measured mx 11.6.6 and 11.15.0, blank apps with a stub PublishedBusinessEvent declaring EventId: 2 errors -> 1 with the attribute dropped, the remaining one being the stub's missing module version folder).
cause: No check compared message attributes with the entity's generalization chain. The entity must declare one attribute per message attribute, an inherited one does not count, and it cannot redeclare an inherited name, so the message can never be satisfied.
fix: In the --references pass, walk the message entity's generalization chain — script-declared entities first, then the project — and report a message attribute whose name (case-insensitive) an ancestor declares, naming the declaring entity. The inherited members are read from the model, not from a list in mxcli; where the chain cannot be read (no BusinessEvents module, unresolvable ancestor) nothing is reported.
test: mdl/executor/validate_business_event_members_test.go (project entity, script entity with case-different name, three silent controls, wiring through validateProgramWithWarnings). Revert control (inherited set forced empty): the three positive tests fail.
insight: mxbuild's wording ('not present on the entity') points at the entity, while the fix is to rename the MESSAGE attribute — say so in the diagnostic. The real marketplace PublishedBusinessEvent's member list was not available here; reading it from the project is what keeps the check right across module versions.
